natural: The priest leaving the altar to replace the cook

meaning.en: To overstep one's role and do another's job.
meaning.zh: 比喻超出自己的职责范围去处理别人的事。

examples.zh: 家长不能越俎代庖，替孩子写作业。
examples.en: Parents shouldn't overstep and do their children's homework for them.

examples.zh: 这是财务部的事，我们不便越俎代庖。
examples.en: That's the finance department's job — we shouldn't step on their toes.

story.en: The hermit Xu You refused the throne offered by Emperor Yao: "Even if the cook does not run the kitchen, the priest does not leave his sacrificial vessels to take his place" (庖人虽不治庖，尸祝不越樽俎而代之矣).
story.zh: 许由拒绝尧让天下："庖人虽不治庖，尸祝不越樽俎而代之矣。"

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: Predicate. 俎 zǔ, 庖 páo.

natural: Misfortunes never come alone

meaning.en: Misfortunes never come singly.
meaning.zh: 指不幸的事接二连三地发生。

equivalents: it never rains but it pours

examples.zh: 真是祸不单行，刚丢了钱包，又淋了一身雨。
examples.en: It never rains but it pours — I lost my wallet and then got soaked.

examples.zh: 福无双至，祸不单行。
examples.en: Blessings never come in pairs, and misfortunes never come alone.

usage.en: Predicate or standalone. Often in 福无双至，祸不单行.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常说"福无双至，祸不单行"。

natural: Without restraint or ties

meaning.en: Free and unrestrained; carefree.
meaning.zh: 没有任何约束，自由自在。

examples.zh: 孩子们在草地上无拘无束地奔跑。
examples.en: The children ran about freely on the grass.

examples.zh: 他喜欢无拘无束的生活。
examples.en: He likes a carefree life.

usage.en: Adverbial or attributive. An idiomatic ABAC.

antonyms: 唐僧念紧箍咒——孙悟空头痛

natural: As firm as a great rock

meaning.en: Rock-solid; unshakeable.
meaning.zh: 像大石头一样坚固。形容不可动摇。

examples.zh: 两国友谊坚如磐石。
examples.en: The friendship between the two countries is rock-solid.

examples.zh: 他的决心坚如磐石。
examples.en: His determination is unshakeable.

natural: Famous with a single success

meaning.en: To become famous overnight with one success.
meaning.zh: 原指科举时代一旦考中就天下闻名。后泛指一下子出了名。

examples.zh: 她凭一首歌一举成名。
examples.en: She shot to fame with a single song.

examples.zh: 这部小说让他一举成名。
examples.en: The novel made him famous overnight.

usage.en: Predicate. In speech 一 is yì.

natural: Open and above board

meaning.en: Open and honest; above board.
meaning.zh: 形容胸怀坦白，正大光明。

examples.zh: 他为人光明磊落，从不搞小动作。
examples.en: He's open and honest and never plays dirty tricks.

examples.zh: 做人要光明磊落。
examples.en: Be upright and above board.

synonyms: 君子坦荡荡，小人长戚戚
antonyms: 又想当婊子又想立牌坊

natural: Lights in ten thousand homes

meaning.en: A city lit up at night; lights in every home.
meaning.zh: 家家户户都亮起了灯。形容城市夜晚的景象。

examples.zh: 站在山顶，看着城市里的万家灯火。
examples.en: From the hilltop we watched the city lights.

examples.zh: 除夕夜，万家灯火，团团圆圆。
examples.en: On New Year's Eve every home is lit up and families are together.

usage.en: Subject or object. Evokes warmth and home.
usage.zh: 多作主语、宾语，带温馨色彩。

natural: Pulling back the raging waves by force

meaning.en: To turn the tide; to save a desperate situation.
meaning.zh: 比喻尽力挽回危险的局势。

equivalents: pull it out of the fire

examples.zh: 最后时刻，他力挽狂澜，帮球队扳平比分。
examples.en: In the dying minutes he turned the tide and helped the team equalise.

examples.zh: 新总裁力挽狂澜，使公司起死回生。
examples.en: The new CEO saved the day and brought the company back from the brink.

story.en: Han Yu praised a scholar who defended Confucianism as one who would "dam the hundred rivers to flow east, and turn back the raging waves after they have broken" (回狂澜于既倒).
story.zh: 韩愈《进学解》："障百川而东之，回狂澜于既倒。"

natural: Stark naked

meaning.en: Completely naked.
meaning.zh: 光着身子，不穿衣服。

examples.zh: 孩子赤身裸体地在河里玩水。
examples.en: The children played in the river stark naked.

examples.zh: 他从浴室出来时几乎赤身裸体。
examples.en: He came out of the bathroom almost naked.

natural: Clever remarks strung like pearls

meaning.en: A stream of witty remarks.
meaning.zh: 巧妙风趣的话一句接一句。

examples.zh: 主持人妙语连珠，全场笑声不断。
examples.en: The host's witticisms kept the audience laughing throughout.

examples.zh: 他的演讲妙语连珠，非常精彩。
examples.en: His speech sparkled with wit.

natural: Having seen much and known widely

meaning.en: Experienced and knowledgeable; worldly-wise.
meaning.zh: 见过的多，知道的广。形容阅历深，经验多。

examples.zh: 爷爷见多识广，什么问题都能回答。
examples.en: Grandpa has seen it all and can answer any question.

examples.zh: 她跑遍了世界各地，见多识广。
examples.en: She's travelled all over the world and is very worldly.

antonyms: 小庙里的和尚——没见过大香火
井蛙不可以语于海者，拘于虚也；夏虫不可以语于冰者，笃于时也
刘姥姥进大观园——少见多怪

natural: Prepared, and so free of trouble

meaning.en: Being prepared averts disaster.
meaning.zh: 事先有防备，就可以避免祸患。

examples.zh: 出门带把伞，有备无患。
examples.en: Take an umbrella — better safe than sorry.

examples.zh: 多存点钱，有备无患。
examples.en: Save a bit more money — it pays to be prepared.

story.en: The Book of Documents: "In every matter there should be preparation; with preparation there is no calamity" (惟事事，乃其有备，有备无患).
story.zh: 《尚书·说命中》："惟事事，乃其有备，有备无患。"

date.zh: 东晋 · 约4世纪初（伪古文《尚书》篇章）
date.en: Eastern Jin, early 4th c. (spurious “Old Text” chapter of the Book of Documents)

antonyms: 平时不烧香，临时抱佛脚

natural: Opening a path of one's own

meaning.en: To blaze a new trail; to find an original approach.
meaning.zh: 独自开辟一条路。比喻独创一种新风格或新方法。

examples.zh: 他在研究中独辟蹊径，取得了突破。
examples.en: He broke new ground in his research and made a breakthrough.

examples.zh: 这家小公司独辟蹊径，专做老年人用品。
examples.en: The small company found its own niche, specialising in products for the elderly.

natural: Little by little becomes a lot

meaning.en: Many a little makes a mickle; small amounts add up.
meaning.zh: 积累少量的东西，能成为大量。

equivalents: many a mickle makes a muckle

examples.zh: 每天背十个单词，积少成多。
examples.en: Learn ten words a day — it all adds up.

examples.zh: 零花钱积少成多，他终于买了自行车。
examples.en: Saving his pocket money little by little, he finally bought a bike.

synonyms: 合抱之木，生于毫末；九层之台，起于累土
antonyms: 狗熊掰包谷——掰一个丢一个

natural: Mind and body both worn out

meaning.en: Mentally and physically exhausted; burnt out.
meaning.zh: 精神和体力都极度劳累。

equivalents: at the end of one's tether

examples.zh: 照顾生病的父亲让她心力交瘁。
examples.en: Caring for her sick father has left her completely burnt out.

examples.zh: 连续加班一个月，他心力交瘁。
examples.en: After a month of overtime, he's utterly drained.

natural: Just come out of the thatched cottage

meaning.en: Inexperienced; just starting out.
meaning.zh: 比喻刚走上社会或刚到工作岗位，缺乏经验。

examples.zh: 他初出茅庐，难免犯些错误。
examples.en: He's just starting out, so he's bound to make some mistakes.

examples.zh: 这位初出茅庐的设计师赢得了大奖。
examples.en: The rookie designer won a major award.

origin.source: 罗贯中《三国演义》第三十九回

story.en: Zhuge Liang, newly come out of his thatched cottage to serve Liu Bei, won his first victory at Bowang Slope — celebrated as "the first exploit after leaving the thatched hut" (初出茅庐第一功).
story.zh: 诸葛亮出山后在博望坡初战告捷，书中称"初出茅庐第一功"。

date.en: late Yuan to early Ming, 14th c.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. Neutral; describes newcomers.

natural: As many as the hairs on an ox

meaning.en: Countless; as many as the hairs on an ox.
meaning.zh: 像牛身上的毛那样多。形容极多。

examples.zh: 网上这类教程多如牛毛。
examples.en: Tutorials like this are ten a penny online.

examples.zh: 当时的苛捐杂税多如牛毛。
examples.en: Taxes and levies at the time were countless.

usage.zh: 多作谓语，常含"太多"之意。

antonyms: 老鼠尾巴上长疖子——有脓也不多

natural: Heart anxious as if scorched by fire

meaning.en: Extremely anxious and impatient.
meaning.zh: 心里急得像火烧一样。形容非常着急。

equivalents: like a cat on hot bricks

examples.zh: 孩子走丢了，妈妈心急火燎地到处找。
examples.en: The child was lost, and his mother searched everywhere frantically.

examples.zh: 他心急火燎地赶往医院。
examples.en: He rushed to the hospital in a frantic state.

usage.en: Adverbial or predicate. 燎 is liǎo here.
usage.zh: 多作状语、谓语。"燎"读 liǎo。

natural: Rowing a boat against the current

meaning.en: Like rowing upstream: if you don't advance, you fall back.
meaning.zh: 逆着水流方向行船。比喻不努力就要后退。

examples.zh: 学如逆水行舟，不进则退。
examples.en: Learning is like rowing upstream — if you don't go forward, you go back.

examples.zh: 在激烈竞争中，企业如逆水行舟。
examples.en: In fierce competition, a business that stands still falls behind.

usage.en: Usually in the saying 学如逆水行舟，不进则退.
usage.zh: 常说"学如逆水行舟，不进则退"。

synonyms: 刀不磨要生锈，人不学要落后
variants: 学如逆水行舟，不进则退

natural: Grafting one flower onto another tree

meaning.en: To pull a switch; to substitute one thing for another by stealth.
meaning.zh: 把一种花木的枝条嫁接到另一种花木上。比喻暗中使用手段，更换人或事物。

examples.zh: 他移花接木，把别人的成果说成自己的。
examples.en: He pulled a switch and passed off someone else's work as his own.

examples.zh: 这段视频是移花接木拼接出来的。
examples.en: The video was spliced together from unrelated footage.

usage.en: Predicate. Literal grafting or (usually) deceptive substitution.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，多指暗中调换。

natural: Passing off fish eyes as pearls

meaning.en: To pass off fakes as genuine; to mix the bad in with the good.
meaning.zh: 拿鱼眼睛冒充珍珠。比喻用假的冒充真的。

equivalents: mix the wheat with the chaff

examples.zh: 市场上鱼目混珠，买古董要小心。
examples.en: The market is full of fakes passed off as genuine — be careful buying antiques.

examples.zh: 有些人鱼目混珠，冒充专家。
examples.en: Some people pass themselves off as experts.

origin.source: 东汉魏伯阳《周易参同契》

story.en: The Cantong qi says that fish eyes are no pearls, yet people pass them off as pearls; the idiom 'mix fish eyes among pearls' is built on this image of fake passing as genuine.
story.zh: 《周易参同契》有“鱼目岂为珠”之语，喻以假充真；后世凝练为“鱼目混珠”。

natural: When drinking water, think of its source

meaning.en: To remember where one's good fortune came from; gratitude to one's benefactors.
meaning.zh: 喝水的时候想起水的来源。比喻不忘本。

equivalents: don't forget where you came from

examples.zh: 他饮水思源，成功后回母校捐建图书馆。
examples.en: Remembering his roots, he funded a library at his old school after making it.

examples.zh: 我们要饮水思源，不忘父母的养育之恩。
examples.en: We should never forget what our parents did for us.

story.en: Yu Xin wrote: "Those who eat the fruit remember the tree; those who drink from the stream cherish its source" (饮其流者怀其源).
story.zh: 庾信《徵调曲》："落其实者思其树，饮其流者怀其源。"

antonyms: 端起碗吃肉，放下筷子骂娘

natural: Glad at others' disasters and pleased at their misfortune

meaning.en: To take pleasure in others' misfortune; schadenfreude.
meaning.zh: 别人遭到灾祸时自己心里高兴。

examples.zh: 同事被批评了，他却幸灾乐祸。
examples.en: When his colleague was told off, he gloated.

examples.zh: 别人遇到困难时，不要幸灾乐祸。
examples.en: Don't take pleasure in other people's troubles.

antonyms: 一根藤上结的苦瓜——苦相连
长太息以掩涕兮，哀民生之多艰

story.en: In the Zuo Commentary, Qing Zheng says that to "take pleasure in others' misfortune" (幸灾) is inhumane (不仁). The idiom 幸灾乐祸 grows out of this condemnation.
story.zh: 《左传·僖公十四年》庆郑说：“幸灾，不仁。”意为以他人灾祸为幸事是不仁的。“幸灾乐祸”由此而来。

natural: Nothing in one's sleeves but a clear breeze

meaning.en: Incorruptible (of an official); having taken nothing improperly.
meaning.zh: 衣袖中除了清风外，别无所有。比喻做官廉洁。

examples.zh: 他当了一辈子官，两袖清风。
examples.en: He was an official all his life and never took a penny.

examples.zh: 人们敬佩这位两袖清风的县长。
examples.en: People admire this incorruptible county head.

story.en: The upright Ming minister Yu Qian refused to bring gifts to court, writing: "With nothing but a clear breeze in my two sleeves I go to court" (清风两袖朝天去).
story.zh: 于谦进京不带礼物，作诗："清风两袖朝天去，免得闾阎话短长。"

usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，多指官员。

antonyms: 吃人家的嘴软，拿人家的手短

natural: Giving up life and forgetting death

meaning.en: To risk one's life without a thought for oneself.
meaning.zh: 不把个人的生死放在心上。

examples.zh: 消防员舍生忘死，冲进火海救人。
examples.en: Risking life and limb, the firefighters charged into the blaze to save people.

examples.zh: 战士们舍生忘死，保卫国家。
examples.en: The soldiers risked everything to defend their country.

synonyms: 苟利国家生死以，岂因祸福避趋之
